newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Netanyahu says peace not doomed despite warnings.
newsitem.headline: Netanyahu says peace not doomed despite warnings.

text.p: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu defended internationally criticised plans to build Jewish housing in Arab East Jerusalem on Tuesday, but said disagreement did not doom the Middle East peace process.

"This kind of doomsday talk and the whole histrionic attitude towards obvious disagreement is itself not conducive to the (peace) process," the visiting Netanyahu told a Moscow news conference with Russia's Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov.
"We have disagreements. We cannot at every stage of this agreement engage in cataclysmic predictions and talk of crisis and violence," he said.
"The important thing is we keep our side of the agreement. We expect the Palestinians to keep theirs and they haven't."
Israeli-Palestinian relations have worsened in recent weeks after an Israeli decision earlier this month to build 6,500 housing units in Arab East Jerusalem.

In addition, the top Palestinian negotiator resigned on Monday following Israel's decision to hand back nine percent of the territory it occupies in the West Bank rather than the 30 percent Palestinians had expected.
"There is a crisis and the crisis is becoming worse and worse," Palestinian Information Minister Yasser Abed Rabbo said.
Netanyahu, on a 48-hour visit to Russia, defended his stance on Tuesday.
"We are not subject to these notions that we have to cede 30 percent or 20 percent of Judea and Samaria to the Palestinian authority," he said.
"There is nothing in the agreement that stipulates this. It says...Israel should determine the extent of these redeployments each time."
"We decided on a nine percent redeployment. By the way, this amounts to a substantial increase to the eight territories allotted to the Palestinians," he added.
On Monday, U.S. President Bill Clinton was the latest in a series of Western and Middle Eastern leaders to condemn the Israeli building plans.
"We're not building a settlement...we're building a neighbourhood in the municipal boundaries of Jerusalem, which is done every day in Amman, in Gaza, in Cairo, and in Moscow.

"It is our responsibility and our right to build in Jerusalem and we will build in Jerusalem," he said. "There is a severe housing shortage in Jerusalem. Young Palestinian couples and young Israeli couples are leaving the city in droves."
The recent tensions have led to increased violence.

At least 10 Palestinians were injured in clashes on Monday when Israeli soldiers used clubs and guns to beat back 100 Palestinians trying to stop workers from opening a road for Jewish settlers near the West Bank city of Hebron.
On Tuesday, an Israeli guard was stabbed 20 times at a Jewish settlement near Hebron.
